## Helper function: getGeneGRanges from Web

```{r getGeneGRanges}
#’ Fetch a GRanges for a given chicken gene symbol (galGal6) via biomaRt
#’
#’ This uses Ensembl’s “ggallus_gene_ensembl” dataset to look up
#’ the chrom, start, end, strand for your gene, collapses across
#’ any transcripts, then optionally extends by upstream/downstream.
#’
#’ @param goi         Gene symbol (character), e.g. "EDA2R"
#’ @param upstream    Bases upstream to include (numeric, default 0)
#’ @param downstream  Bases downstream to include (numeric, default 0)
#’ @return A single GRanges object spanning the gene body ± flanks
#’ @importFrom GenomicRanges GRanges IRanges
#’ @importFrom biomaRt useEnsembl getBM
#’ @examples
#’ gr <- getGeneGRanges("EDA2R", upstream=1000, downstream=1000)
#’ CoveragePlot(..., region=gr, ...)
getGeneGRanges <- function(goi, upstream=0, downstream=0) {
  if (!requireNamespace("biomaRt", quietly=TRUE)) {
    stop("Please install the biomaRt package: BiocManager::install('biomaRt')")
  }
  library(biomaRt)
  library(GenomicRanges)
  
  # connect to Ensembl Genes for chicken
  ensembl <- useEnsembl(
    biomart="genes", 
    dataset="ggallus_gene_ensembl"
  )  
  
  # fetch chrom, start, end, strand for all transcripts of goi
  attrs <- c("chromosome_name","start_position","end_position","strand")
  res <- getBM(
    attributes = attrs,
    filters    = "external_gene_name",
    values     = goi,
    mart       = ensembl
  )
  if (nrow(res)==0) {
    stop(sprintf("Gene ‘%s’ not found in Ensembl ggallus_gene_ensembl", goi))
  }
  
  # collapse across transcripts to full gene span
  seqs <- unique(res$chromosome_name)
  if (length(seqs)!=1) {
    stop("Gene spans multiple chromosomes; please check annotation.")
  }
  gr <- GRanges(
    seqnames = seqs,
    ranges   = IRanges(
      start = min(res$start_position),
      end   = max(res$end_position)
    ),
    strand   = if (all(res$strand==1)) "+" else if (all(res$strand==2)) "-" else "*"
  )
  
  # extend by flanking bases
  if (upstream>0 || downstream>0) {
    start(gr) <- pmax(1, start(gr) - upstream)
    end(gr)   <- end(gr)   + downstream
  }
  return(gr)
}
``` 

## Parameters for gene sets and flanking, modifided top and bottom genes, MSX1 added for reference  

```{r parameters}
#gene lists from combined_differential, Added MSX1.
top_genes    <- c("FABP9","ARC","ENSGALG00010020695","TUBB6","TGFB2","S100A6",
                  "TMEM158","KLF2","HSPB1","ARPC1B","ADCYAP1","MSX1")
bottom_genes <- c("GLUL","PADI3","UTS2B","GFAP","CPXM2",
                  "APCDD1","WIF1","G6PC2","CA2","ENSGALG00010007547")

# define how many bases to flank each gene
flank.up   <- 1000
flank.down <- 1000

# initialize lists to store plots
top_cov_plot       <- list()
top_expr_plot    <- list()

bottom_cov_plot    <- list()
bottom_expr_plot <- list()
``` 

## Generate plots for top genes

```{r top-gene-plots}
for (goi in top_genes) {
  cat("Generating plots for:", goi, "\n")
  region_gr <- if (goi == "ENSGALG00010020695") {
    GRanges(
  "33",
  IRanges(start = 11847635, end = 11851020)
)
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  try({
    if (is.null(region_gr)) {
      region_gr <- getGeneGRanges(goi, upstream=flank.up, downstream=flank.down)
    }
    expr_plot <- ExpressionPlot(object=rna, features=goi, assay="RNA", group.by="predicted_celltype")
    cov_plot  <- CoveragePlot(object=atac, region=region_gr, annotation=TRUE, peaks=TRUE,
                              links=TRUE, assay="ATAC", group.by="celltype",
                              extend.upstream=flank.up, extend.downstream=flank.down)
    top_expr_plot[[goi]] <- expr_plot
    top_cov_plot[[goi]]  <- cov_plot
  }, silent=FALSE)
}

```

## Display all plots

```{r display-plots}

# Helper to place coverage on the left and expression on the right
# using wrap_plots with explicit widths, converting tracks to ggplots
library(ggplotify)
side_by_side <- function(cov, expr, widths = c(3, 1)) {
  # convert coverage Track to ggplot object
  cov_gg <- as.ggplot(cov)
  # ensure expr is ggplot
  expr_gg <- expr
  wrap_plots(cov_gg, expr_gg, ncol = 2, widths = widths)
}

# Display top genes side-by-side
for (goi in top_genes) {
  expr_plot <- top_expr_plot[[goi]]
  cov_plot  <- top_cov_plot [[goi]]
  cat("Rendering gene (side-by-side):", goi, "\n")
  p <- side_by_side(cov_plot, expr_plot, widths = c(3, 1))
  print(p)
}

# Display bottom genes side-by-side
for (goi in bottom_genes) {
  expr_plot <- bottom_expr_plot[[goi]]
  cov_plot  <- bottom_cov_plot [[goi]]
  cat("Rendering gene (side-by-side):", goi, "\n")
  p <- side_by_side(cov_plot, expr_plot, widths = c(3, 1))
  print(p)
}
```



# Adds Motifs, Lots of Conversions Needed Since Peks dont match latest JASPAR
```{r motif-analysis, print=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(Seurat)            # v5+
library(Signac)            # >=1.9.0
library(JASPAR2020)
library(TFBSTools)
library(BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6)
library(GenomeInfoDb)
library(GenomicRanges)

# ——— 1. Load your ATAC object ———
atac <- readRDS("atac_prePlot.rds")
DefaultAssay(atac) <- "ATAC"
atac <- RegionStats(object = atac, genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6)

# ——— 2. Rebuild & clean up peak GRanges ———
peak_names  <- rownames(atac@assays$ATAC@counts)
peak_ranges <- StringToGRanges(peak_names, sep = c(":", "-"))
names(peak_ranges) <- peak_names

genome_si   <- seqinfo(BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6)
seqlevelsStyle(peak_ranges) <- seqlevelsStyle(genome_si)
keep_lvls   <- intersect(seqlevels(peak_ranges), standardChromosomes(genome_si))
peak_ranges <- keepSeqlevels(peak_ranges, keep_lvls, pruning.mode = "coarse")
seqinfo(peak_ranges) <- genome_si[keep_lvls]
peak_ranges <- trim(peak_ranges)

# ——— 3. Subset your counts to match those trimmed ranges ———
counts_trimmed <- atac@assays$ATAC@counts[ names(peak_ranges), , drop = FALSE ]
stopifnot(
  nrow(counts_trimmed) == length(peak_ranges),
  all(rownames(counts_trimmed) == names(peak_ranges))
)

# Grab any existing fragments path
frag_path <- atac@assays$ATAC@fragments %||% NULL

# ——— 4. Create a brand‐new peaks ChromatinAssay ———
atac[["peaks"]] <- CreateChromatinAssay(
  counts    = counts_trimmed,
  ranges    = peak_ranges,
  genome    = "galGal6",
  sep       = c(":", "-"),
  fragments = frag_path
)

DefaultAssay(atac) <- "peaks"

atac <- RegionStats(
  object = atac,
  assay  = "peaks",
  genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6
)

message(
  "New ‘peaks’ assay: ",
  nrow(atac@assays$peaks@counts), " peaks × ",
  ncol(atac@assays$peaks@counts), " cells\n"
)

# ——— 5. Load JASPAR2020 PFMs ———
opts <- list(species = 9606, all_versions = FALSE)
pfm <- getMatrixSet(JASPAR2020, opts)
message("Loaded ", length(pfm), " PWMs from JASPAR2020.\n")

# ——— 6. Add motifs & run chromVAR ———
# Signac will matchMotifs(), subset/alignto your ‘peaks’ assay, and attach them
atac <- AddMotifs(
  object = atac,
  genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6,
  pfm    = pfm
)

matched_peaks <- rownames(atac@assays$peaks@motifs@data)
message("Keeping ", length(matched_peaks), " peaks that have motif data.")

# 2) Pull out the trimmed counts & ranges you originally built
orig_counts   <- atac@assays$peaks@counts
orig_ranges   <- atac@assays$peaks@ranges
frag_path     <- atac@assays$peaks@fragments %||% NULL


# Force names to match counts matrix
names(orig_ranges) <- rownames(orig_counts)

# Now subset in lockstep
counts_matched <- orig_counts[matched_peaks, , drop = FALSE]
ranges_matched <- orig_ranges[matched_peaks]

# Confirm match
stopifnot(
  nrow(counts_matched) == length(ranges_matched),
  all(rownames(counts_matched) == names(ranges_matched))
)

# 3) Subset both in lockstep
counts_matched <- orig_counts[matched_peaks, , drop = FALSE]
ranges_matched <- orig_ranges[matched_peaks]
stopifnot(
  nrow(counts_matched) == length(ranges_matched),
  all(rownames(counts_matched) == names(ranges_matched))
)

# 4) Create a brand‐new ChromatinAssay
new_peaks_assay <- CreateChromatinAssay(
  counts    = counts_matched,
  ranges    = ranges_matched,
  genome    = "galGal6",
  sep       = c(":", "-"),
  fragments = frag_path
)

atac[["peaks"]] <- new_peaks_assay
DefaultAssay(atac) <- "peaks"
atac <- AddMotifs(
  object = atac,
  genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6,
  pfm    = pfm
)

message("Rebuilt 'peaks' assay with matched counts & ranges.")

# 6) Re‐attach your motifs slot (Signac will re‐use the existing motif object)
motif_obj <- atac@assays$peaks@motifs
atac@assays$peaks@motifs <- motif_obj

# 7) Now RunChromVAR() on this clean assay
DefaultAssay(atac) <- "peaks"
atac <- RunChromVAR(
  object = atac,
  genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6
)
message("chromVAR completed on ", nrow(atac@assays$peaks@counts), " peaks.")

```
#Plots and Save top motifs 
```{r}
## ——— Bottom section: motif‐enrichment with proper GC‐matching ———

# 1) Make sure we're using the peaks assay
DefaultAssay(atac) <- "peaks"

# 2) Read in your DA peaks and convert to peak names in the object
da_peaks <- read.csv("da_peaks.csv", row.names = 1)
filtered_da_peaks <- da_peaks[da_peaks$p_val_adj < 0.05 & da_peaks$avg_log2FC > 0.5, ]

peak_names <- rownames(filtered_da_peaks)
converted_peak_names <- paste0("chr", peak_names)            # assume your rownames are e.g. "1-2345-2450"
converted_peak_names <- intersect(converted_peak_names, rownames(atac))

# 3) Drop any old GC.percent or sequence.length columns
mf <- atac@assays$peaks@meta.features
mf <- mf[, !colnames(mf) %in% c("GC.percent", "sequence.length")]
atac@assays$peaks@meta.features <- mf

# 4) Recompute GC‐ and size‐bias metrics
atac <- RegionStats(
  object = atac,
  assay  = "peaks",
  genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6
)

# 5) Rename to the Signac‐expected slot names so that FindMotifs() can draw a GC‐matched
mf <- atac@assays$peaks@meta.features
mf$gc           <- mf$GC.percent
mf$bias         <- mf$sequence.length
mf$region.width <- mf$sequence.length
atac@assays$peaks@meta.features <- mf

# 6) (Re‐)add motifs (will reuse the existing motif object if present)
atac <- AddMotifs(
  object = atac,
  genome = BSgenome.Ggallus.UCSC.galGal6,
  pfm    = pfm
)

# 7) Run motif enrichment with automatic GC‐matched background
enriched <- FindMotifs(
  object   = atac,
  features = converted_peak_names
)

# 8) Sort by p‐value (ascending) and write out
enriched_sorted <- enriched[order(enriched$pvalue), ]
head(enriched_sorted)

write.csv(
  enriched_sorted,
  "enriched_motifs_sorted.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

#save updated Seurat object
saveRDS(atac, "atac_with_motifs_and_stats.rds")

#example plot
p2 <- FeaturePlot(
  object = atac,
  features = "MA1513.1",
  min.cutoff = 'q10',
  max.cutoff = 'q90',
  pt.size = 0.1
)

p2

```


## Future Analysis

#### Future Analysis will likely combine more multimodal data to observe the differences between Activated/Resting Muller Glia or other identified types or clusters with the treatments of saline and NMDA. This could be done by stitching more rna/atac samples into the original objects (like has been done in RNA_ATAC_Setup), or via true multiomic analysis in the same cells. Different Cell type Clustering/Labeling Or Dimensions methods can also be tried.
